name: clean-up-crew
description: Check Windows disk usage across the system drive, report growth trends, and clean approved caches safely. Use for "check C drive", "clean up disk", "clean up C", "disk is full", "what is using my space", "find large files", "weekly disk check", "what can I delete", or /clean-up-crew.

# Clean Up Crew

Safely audit and clean a Windows system drive.

It covers the whole system drive in two ways: an allowlist of safe junk locations (developer caches, browser caches, temp, crash dumps, update caches, Recycle Bin) and an optional deep scan that finds the largest files and old installers outside Windows, Program Files, and protected system folders. The deep scan is report-only; those files are never deleted by a plan.

- Skill ID: `clean-up-crew`
- Command: `/clean-up-crew`
- Base directory: the folder that contains this `SKILL.md`. Use its absolute path wherever the examples show `<skill-base>`.
- Slash command: Antigravity generates `/clean-up-crew` from the skill name. OpenCode needs `command.md` copied to `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\commands\clean-up-crew.md`; without it, the skill still works when described in natural language. The argument routing in `command.md` is OpenCode-only; on other agents, ask in plain language, for example "build the recommended cleanup plan".
- Installed locations: OpenCode `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\skills\clean-up-crew`; Antigravity App and IDE `~/.gemini/config/skills/clean-up-crew`; Antigravity CLI `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/clean-up-crew`; agents that use the shared convention read `.agents/skills/clean-up-crew` per project, with global paths that vary by agent. See `README.md` for the install commands.
- Reporting is read-only. `Get-DiskReport.ps1 -SaveHistory` also appends one local history record.
- Deletion happens only through a plan generated by the bundled scripts and approved in the current conversation.

## Hard rules

- Never delete anything without explicit approval in the current conversation.
- Never invent cleanup paths. The allowlist in `references/targets.json` is authoritative.
- Never touch user documents, the registry, restore points, `pagefile.sys`, `hiberfil.sys`, or `swapfile.sys` directly.
- Stay out of `Windows\`, `Program Files\`, `Program Files (x86)\`, and `WinSxS`, except the explicitly allowlisted targets: `%SystemRoot%\Temp`, `%SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download`, `%SystemRoot%\Minidump\*.dmp`, `%SystemRoot%\LiveKernelReports\*.dmp`, and `%SystemRoot%\MEMORY.DMP`.
- Deep-scan results, including large files, old installers, and top folders, are review-only. Never delete them as part of a plan and never present them as cleanup targets.
- Do not edit `references/targets.json` between planning and applying. `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1` re-expands paths from that file, so an edit changes what an approved plan deletes.
- Wildcards in `targets.json` are expanded to concrete paths before planning and again before applying. Every expanded path must pass the path guard. Never add a wildcard that can resolve into a protected path.
- `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1` requires `-Apply`; never pass `-Apply` unless the user approved that exact plan.
- If an item is blocked (browser running, admin required), report it. Never force-kill processes.
- Never use `DISM /ResetBase` from this skill. It is a separate, explicitly consented decision.
- Never escalate to riskier deletions because the freed space was less than expected.

## Scripts and flags

| Script | Purpose | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/Get-DiskReport.ps1` | Report free space, target sizes, top folders, trend, recommendations. No deletion. | `-SaveHistory`, `-Json`, `-SkipTopDirs`, `-IncludeDism`, `-DeepScan`, `-LargeFileMB <n>`, `-OldInstallerDays <n>`, `-TopDirs <n>` |
| `scripts/New-CleanupPlan.ps1` | Resolve target IDs and blocked status into a plan JSON. No deletion. | `-Items <id,...>`, `-AllTier1`, `-Preset recommended`, `-OutFile <path>`, `-Json` |
| `scripts/Invoke-Cleanup.ps1` | Dry-run a plan or apply it, verify results, append history. | `-PlanFile <path>`, `-Apply`, `-Json` |
| `scripts/Get-Trend.ps1` | Read history and calculate growth rate and runway. | `-Last <n>`, `-Json`, `-HistoryFile <path>` |
| `tests/Test-Guardrails.ps1` | Verify path guardrails and deletion exclusions. | none |
| `tests/Test-Apply.ps1` | End-to-end apply test with a fixture target, history isolation, and trend check. | none |

`-IncludeDism` adds a `componentStore` field. When elevated it runs `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore`; otherwise the field is `{ Error = 'requires administrator' }` and the rest of the report still runs. `-TopDirs` defaults to 8.

`-DeepScan` walks the system drive and adds three review-only blocks to the report: top-level folder sizes, files of at least `-LargeFileMB` (default 250) outside Windows, Program Files, `$Recycle.Bin`, `System Volume Information`, and `Recovery`, and installers older than `-OldInstallerDays` (default 90) at the top level of Downloads and Desktop. It takes several minutes and deletes nothing. The same data appears in the JSON `deepScan` object.

`-Preset recommended` selects every tier-1 target except `recycle-bin`. `-AllTier1` selects every tier-1 target, including the Recycle Bin.

Run scripts with:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<skill-base>\scripts\Get-DiskReport.ps1" -SaveHistory
```

## Workflow

### 1. Report (default)

Run `Get-DiskReport.ps1 -SaveHistory`. Add `-SkipTopDirs` for a faster report, or `-Json` when another tool will parse the output. Add `-DeepScan` when the user asks what is using the drive, asks for large files, or wants a general cleanup; it takes several minutes.

Present a compact summary:

- free GB and percent
- cleanup targets: id, tier, size, ready/blocked
- top `LocalAppData` folders and top global npm packages
- deep-scan review blocks when requested: top folders, large files, old installers
- trend: GB/week and weeks until 2 GB remain
- recommendations

Do not delete anything in this step. Ask which target IDs the user approves. For a general cleanup, recommend `-Preset recommended`, which covers every tier-1 target except the Recycle Bin. Approval must name IDs or a tier, not "clean everything". The sizes are measurements at report time; the plan re-measures them.

### 2. Plan

For the approved IDs:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<skill-base>\scripts\New-CleanupPlan.ps1" `
  -Items npm-cache,chrome-cache -OutFile "$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json"
```

Use `-Preset recommended` for a general cleanup, or `-AllTier1` to select every tier-1 target including the Recycle Bin. `New-CleanupPlan.ps1` does not delete and does not run the path guard. It records the selected IDs, current sizes, and blocked status (process/admin). The `paths` in the plan are informational; apply ignores them and re-expands from `targets.json`. Wildcards in `targets.json` are expanded during both steps.

Show the plan: item, size, status, and blocked reasons. If an item is blocked, ask the user to close the named app or to run elevated, then regenerate the plan. Blocked items stay in the plan and are skipped at apply.

Generated plans carry `createdAt`. `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1 -Apply` rejects plans older than one hour. It cannot detect a restart or a target change; regenerate after either.

`dism-component-cleanup` has no byte estimate and reports 0 bytes. Use `-IncludeDism` in the report for component-store analysis; apply can take 10-30 minutes.

### 3. Apply

Only after the user explicitly approves the plan in this conversation:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<skill-base>\scripts\Invoke-Cleanup.ps1" `
  -PlanFile "$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json" -Apply
```

The script re-expands every path from `targets.json`, runs the path guard, re-checks blocked processes and admin state, skips blocked items, measures bytes before and after for file targets, and appends one `apply` record to history. Use `-Json` for a machine-readable result with `freeBeforeGB`, `freeAfterGB`, `freedBytes`, `failed`, `items`, and `errors`.

Per-item `freedBytes` is measured for file-based targets. Recycle Bin and DISM report 0 per item; use `freeBeforeGB` and `freeAfterGB` for the net result.

### 4. Verify

Run the report again with `-SaveHistory` and report:

- free space before and after
- bytes actually freed per item, where measured
- failures or skipped items
- any target that regrew immediately

For a preview without deleting, run `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1 -PlanFile <path>` without `-Apply`. A dry run does not run DISM or measure the Recycle Bin; both can show `nothing to delete` even when work is pending.

### 5. Trend

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<skill-base>\scripts\Get-Trend.ps1" -Last 8
```

`-Last` defaults to 8 entries; values below 2 are treated as 2. Growth is calculated from the first and last entry in that window, using only entries that have a numeric `freeGB`. Both the report's trend block and `Get-Trend.ps1` apply that filter. Use `-HistoryFile <path>` to read an alternate history file in tests.

History is written only by `Get-DiskReport.ps1 -SaveHistory` and by `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1 -Apply`. Plain reports do not add entries. Apply records store the post-apply free space as `freeGB`. Because history mixes report and apply records, a large cleanup can skew the growth rate.

## Tiers

| Tier | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Safe cleanup; low risk | npm, pnpm, pip, uv, Yarn, Bun, Deno, Cargo, Gradle, Maven, NuGet, Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Brave caches, Temp, crash dumps, error reports, Windows Update cache, Recycle Bin |
| 2 | System-level; slower or loses diagnostics, needs admin | DISM component cleanup, Windows crash dumps |
| 3 | Trade-offs; never executed by this skill | hibernation, pagefile size, uninstalling apps |

Tier values live in `targets.json`. Tier 1 means low risk to the system, not zero data loss: crash dumps, error reports, and the Recycle Bin remove diagnostic data or files permanently. `recycle-bin` is tier 1 for grouping but is irreversible, so `-Preset recommended` excludes it. Tier 3 items are not targets; they are recommendations only. Discuss them and get separate consent; do not delete or change them with these scripts.

## Target IDs

The authoritative list is `references/targets.json`. These groups are a convenience snapshot; trust the JSON if they disagree.

- **Developer and tool caches:** `npm-cache`, `pnpm-store`, `yarn-cache`, `pip-cache`, `uv-cache`, `bun-cache`, `deno-cache`, `go-build-cache`, `cargo-cache`, `gradle-cache`, `maven-repo`, `nuget-cache`, `cpptools-ipch`, `electron-cache`, `lm-studio-updater`, `google-updater-cache`
- **Browser caches:** `chrome-cache`, `edge-cache`, `firefox-cache`, `brave-cache`
- **Temp and reports:** `temp-user`, `temp-windows`, `crash-dumps-user`, `wer-user`, `wer-system`
- **Windows updates:** `windows-update-cache`, `delivery-optimization-cache`
- **Special:** `recycle-bin` (irreversible), `crash-dumps-system` (tier 2), `dism-component-cleanup` (tier 2)

## Reporting guidance

- Lead with free GB and percent.
- Distinguish verified growth (target sizes) from general system churn.
- Call out the largest non-cache blocks (hibernation, pagefile, big apps) separately.
- State what will regrow; do not imply cleanup is permanent.
- Do not present the sum of target bytes as guaranteed free space. Per-item measurements can overstate the net gain.
- If growth exceeds roughly 0.3 GB/week, mention the runway to 2 GB free.
- Deep-scan rows are review-only. Say that explicitly; never count them toward cleanup totals or imply that approving a plan deletes them.
- When a deep-scan large file is also inside a cleanup target, label it as removable through that target; otherwise it is a manual review item.

## Troubleshooting

- Execution policy: always invoke with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`.
- Admin: `temp-windows`, `wer-system`, `windows-update-cache`, `delivery-optimization-cache`, `crash-dumps-system`, and `dism-component-cleanup` are blocked without elevation. Do not work around it.
- Hibernation file: without elevation the report cannot read its size and shows `enabled; exact size needs admin` instead.
- Locked files: `Remove-CleanupContents` skips them and reports failures. Close the app and retry; do not force-delete.
- Browser caches: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Brave must be closed. Ask first; never kill the process.
- Missing target: a missing directory or unmatched wildcard is normal and is treated as zero bytes.
- Deep scan: takes several minutes on a full drive and is report-only. Do not run it on every routine check; use it when the user asks where the space went or wants a general cleanup.
- Windows.old: the report only recommends removal through Settings or Disk Cleanup. This skill does not delete it.
- DISM target: reports 0 bytes by design, so the report can show it as `empty`; use `-IncludeDism` for component-store analysis and expect a long apply. A plan can show `nothing to delete` for this target; that is a size artifact, not a no-op.
- Recycle Bin and DISM: per-item freed bytes stay 0; use the net free-space delta.
- Plan age: `-Apply` rejects plans older than one hour. Regenerate after a restart or a `targets.json` change.
- History: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode-disk-cleanup\history.jsonl`; one JSON object per saved report or apply.

## References

- `references/targets.json` - allowlist and target metadata.
- `references/safety-rules.md` - protected paths, consent model, deletion mechanics.
- `references/report-template.md` - report layout.

## Change management

Add a target to `references/targets.json` only with: `id`, `name`, `tier`, `type`, `paths`, `exclude`, `processes`, `requiresAdmin`, `regenerates`, and `risk`. Supported types are `contents` (delete children of each path), `files` (delete each matched file, which may be a wildcard), `profile-caches`, `recyclebin`, and `dism`. For `profile-caches`, also provide `profileRoot`, `profilePattern`, and `cacheDirs`; `extraPaths` is optional. For `dism` and `recyclebin`, `paths` is empty. Wildcards are allowed in `contents` and `files` paths and are resolved before planning and applying. Run both scripts in `tests/` after edits.

# Clean Up Crew

[![Tests](https://github.com/peterhany4/clean-up-crew/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/peterhany4/clean-up-crew/actions/workflows/test.yml)

A crew of agent skills for Windows disk cleanup and safe maintenance.

The first skill, **`clean-up-crew`**, audits disk usage across the Windows system drive, builds a cleanup plan, and deletes only after you approve that exact plan. It covers developer and browser caches, temp files, crash dumps, Windows Update caches, and the Recycle Bin. An optional deep scan shows the largest files and old installers outside Windows and Program Files, but never deletes them. It never force-kills processes and never works around administrator requirements.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11
- PowerShell 5.1+ (included with Windows)
- An agent that supports the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) standard, such as OpenCode, Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
- Optional: Node.js 18+ if you want to install with `npx skills`

## Install

The skill follows the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) standard, so the same folder works in any compatible agent. Pick one install path per agent.

| Agent | Install | `/clean-up-crew` |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | `npx skills` with `-a opencode` | copy `command.md` |
| Antigravity App or IDE | skill folder in `~/.gemini/config/skills` | automatic |
| Antigravity CLI | `agy plugin install <repo>` | automatic |
| Other agents | `npx skills` with `-a <agent>` | varies by agent |

### OpenCode

```powershell
npx skills add peterhany4/clean-up-crew --skill clean-up-crew -g -a opencode -y --copy
```

The skills CLI installs skills, not slash commands. The command template ships inside the installed skill. This finds it whether the skill was installed globally by the CLI or copied manually:

```powershell
$skillDir = @(
    "$env:USERPROFILE\.agents\skills\clean-up-crew",
    "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\skills\clean-up-crew"
) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $_ 'command.md') } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $skillDir) { throw 'clean-up-crew skill not found. Run the install step first.' }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\commands" | Out-Null
Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $skillDir 'command.md') "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\commands\clean-up-crew.md" -Force
```

Restart OpenCode if needed, then run `/clean-up-crew` or ask it to "check C drive".

### Antigravity

The repository root is also a valid Antigravity plugin (`plugin.json` with `skills/clean-up-crew` inside). The CLI installs it, including the skill:

```powershell
agy plugin install https://github.com/peterhany4/clean-up-crew
```

For the Antigravity App or IDE, copy the skill folder into the global skills directory:

```powershell
$dest = "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini\config\skills\clean-up-crew"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini\config\skills" | Out-Null
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dest -Recurse -Force }
Copy-Item -LiteralPath .\skills\clean-up-crew -Destination $dest -Recurse -Force
```

Or use the skills CLI, which writes to the Antigravity CLI path:

```powershell
npx skills add peterhany4/clean-up-crew --skill clean-up-crew -g -a antigravity-cli -y --copy
```

Antigravity turns the skill into `/clean-up-crew` automatically. The `clean`, `deep`, and `plan` argument routing in `command.md` is OpenCode-only; on Antigravity, ask in plain language, for example "build the recommended cleanup plan".

### Other agents

```powershell
npx skills add peterhany4/clean-up-crew --skill clean-up-crew -g -a claude-code -y --copy
```

Swap `claude-code` for `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `windsurf`, or run with `--agent '*'`. Run `npx skills add peterhany4/clean-up-crew --list` to browse before installing.

### Update later

```powershell
npx skills update clean-up-crew -g
```

For an Antigravity plugin install, run `agy plugin uninstall clean-up-crew` and install it again.

## What it does

- Reports free space, 30 cleanup target sizes, top `LocalAppData` folders, top global npm packages, and growth trend.
- Covers developer caches (npm, pnpm, Yarn, pip, uv, Bun, Deno, Cargo, Gradle, Maven, NuGet, and more), browser caches (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave), temp folders, crash dumps, error reports, and Windows Update caches.
- Builds a JSON plan for the target IDs you approve, or a general plan with `-Preset recommended` (all tier-1 targets except the Recycle Bin).
- Applies only that plan, re-checking paths and blocked processes at apply time.
- `-DeepScan` adds a review-only map of the drive: top folders, files of 250 MB or more outside Windows, Program Files, and protected system folders, and installers older than 90 days at the top level of Downloads and Desktop. Nothing in that list is deleted.
- Handles blocked browser caches and admin-only targets without force-killing or escalating.
- Treats hibernation, pagefile changes, and app uninstalls as recommendations only (Tier 3).

## Safety model

- **Report** is read-only. With `-SaveHistory` it adds one local history record. `-DeepScan` is also read-only and only lists review candidates.
- **Plan** changes nothing. It records target IDs, current sizes, and blocked status. `-Preset recommended` excludes the irreversible Recycle Bin.
- **Apply** requires explicit approval of the exact plan. The scripts re-expand paths from `references/targets.json`, re-check the path guard and blocked processes, and skip blocked items.
- The scripts never force-kill processes or work around administrator requirements.
- Deep-scan large files and old installers are never treated as targets. The user must review and remove them manually.
- History lives at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode-disk-cleanup\history.jsonl`. It is personal data and is not included in this repository.

## Manual install (OpenCode)

If you do not want to use the skills CLI, download or clone this repository and run the following from the repository root:

```powershell
$dest = "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\skills\clean-up-crew"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\skills" | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\commands" | Out-Null
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dest -Recurse -Force }
Copy-Item -LiteralPath .\skills\clean-up-crew -Destination $dest -Recurse -Force
Copy-Item -LiteralPath .\skills\clean-up-crew\command.md -Destination "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\commands\clean-up-crew.md" -Force
```

If the repository was downloaded as a zip, unblock it first:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath . -Recurse -File | Unblock-File
```

Or right-click the zip, open Properties, select **Unblock**, then extract it.

## Verify

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\skills\clean-up-crew\tests\Test-Guardrails.ps1
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\skills\clean-up-crew\tests\Test-Apply.ps1
```

Expected: 20 guardrail passes and 18 apply passes. The apply test uses temporary fixtures and restores `targets.json` and the local history file.

## Repository layout

- `plugin.json` - Antigravity plugin manifest; makes the repository installable with `agy plugin install`.
- `assets/logo.svg` - plugin icon.
- `skills/clean-up-crew/SKILL.md` - workflow and safety rules.
- `skills/clean-up-crew/command.md` - `/clean-up-crew` slash command template for OpenCode.
- `skills/clean-up-crew/references/targets.json` - allowlisted cleanup targets.
- `skills/clean-up-crew/scripts/` - report, plan, apply, and trend scripts.
- `skills/clean-up-crew/tests/` - guardrail and end-to-end tests.

## Customizing

Add or remove targets in `skills/clean-up-crew/references/targets.json`. Keep the required fields and run both tests after edits. Wildcards are supported in `contents` and `files` paths; each match is guarded at apply time.

The skill targets the Windows system drive and uses `%SystemRoot%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, and `%SystemDrive%`, so it adapts to the system drive letter. The deep scan follows the same system drive.

### Target types

| Type | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `contents` | Deletes the children of each directory; keeps the directory itself. |
| `files` | Deletes each exact file or wildcard match. Never recurses into a directory. |
| `profile-caches` | Expands browser profile directories and deletes the listed cache subfolders. |
| `recyclebin` | Clears the Recycle Bin for the system drive. Irreversible. |
| `dism` | Runs `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup`. |

## More skills

The `clean-up-crew` skill is the first member of the crew. New Windows maintenance skills can live under `skills/` without changing the install command for existing skills.

description: Check Windows disk usage and clean approved caches safely across the system drive
---

Load the `clean-up-crew` skill with the `skill` tool. The skill is authoritative for safety, targets, and script behavior. This command maps the user's arguments to one step of that workflow.

User arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

## Routing

| Arguments | Action |
|---|---|
| empty, `report`, `status` | Run `Get-DiskReport.ps1 -SaveHistory`; present the report. Do not create a plan. |
| `deep`, `scan` | Run `Get-DiskReport.ps1 -SaveHistory -DeepScan`; present the report and the review-only large-file and installer list. Do not create a plan. |
| `clean`, `general` | Run `Get-DiskReport.ps1 -SaveHistory`, then `New-CleanupPlan.ps1 -Preset recommended`; show the report and plan. Stop for approval. |
| `trend` | Run `Get-Trend.ps1 -Last 8`; summarize growth and runway. |
| `targets`, `list` | List target IDs from the skill's `references/targets.json` with tier, name, and risk. Read-only. |
| `plan <id> [<id> ...]` | Run `New-CleanupPlan.ps1 -Items <ids> -OutFile "$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json"`; show the plan. Stop. |
| `plan recommended` | Run `New-CleanupPlan.ps1 -Preset recommended -OutFile "$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json"`; show the plan. Stop. |
| `plan tier1` | Run `New-CleanupPlan.ps1 -AllTier1 -OutFile "$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json"`; show the plan, including the irreversible Recycle Bin. Stop. |
| `dry-run [plan-path]` | Run `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1 -PlanFile <path>` without `-Apply`. Default path: `$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json`. |
| `apply [plan-path]` | Only with explicit approval of that exact plan; run `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1 -PlanFile <path> -Apply`. Default path: `$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json`. |
| bare target IDs | Treat as `plan <ids>`. |

If `<plan-path>` is omitted for `dry-run` or `apply`, use `$env:TEMP\clean-up-crew-plan.json`. If that file does not exist, run `plan` first; do not guess target IDs. If the request is ambiguous, ask one question. Do not infer approval from a prior "ok", "go ahead", or "clean it" that was not tied to a shown plan.

## Non-negotiable rules

- For a new cleanup, report first unless the user named specific target IDs. Never plan and apply in one step. For `clean`, run the report and plan in one turn but stop before applying.
- Approval must identify the plan (plan ID, or the exact target IDs/tier and sizes shown in this conversation). "Clean everything" is not approval.
- `-Preset recommended` excludes the Recycle Bin. `-AllTier1` includes it; say that it is irreversible before asking for approval.
- Deep-scan large files and old installers are review-only. Never add them to a plan or delete them.
- Never pass `-Apply` without that approval.
- Never edit the skill's `references/targets.json` to bypass a block or to add a path.
- Never force-kill a process. If a browser or other listed process is running, report it and ask the user to close it.
- Never work around an administrator requirement or retry with elevation silently.
- Recycle Bin cleanup is irreversible; say so before asking for approval.
- If a plan is older than one hour, regenerate it. Do not reuse a stale plan.
- After an apply, stop. Report the result; do not chain another deletion.

## Response shape

1. **Report**: free GB and percent, target table, largest consumers, trend, recommendations. Include deep-scan review blocks when `-DeepScan` ran.
2. **Plan**: plan ID, target IDs with measured size and status, blocked reasons, what will regrow, explicit approval question.
3. **Apply result**: per-item freed bytes where measured, net free-space delta from `freeBeforeGB`/`freeAfterGB`, failures and skipped items, any immediate regrowth.
4. **Trend**: free-space change per week and runway to 2 GB.

Keep it compact. Distinguish measured bytes from estimates and net free-space change from measured deletions.

# Disk report template

Use measured values from `Get-DiskReport.ps1`. Do not fill gaps with estimates.

## Status

- Drive: `C:`
- Free: `X.XX GB` (`XX.X%`)
- Change since last check: `+/-X.XX GB` (from history; `n/a` on first run)

## Cleanup targets

| ID | Tier | Size | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|
| npm-cache | 1 | 0.00 GB | ready |

# Safety rules

## Consent model

1. **Report** is read-only. It measures sizes and, with `-SaveHistory`, appends one history record. `-DeepScan` also walks the drive for review-only large files and old installers.
2. **Plan** is read-only. It resolves allowlisted targets, measures current sizes, and records blocked status. It does not delete and does not run the path guard. `-Preset recommended` selects every tier-1 target except `recycle-bin`; `-AllTier1` includes it.
3. **Apply** requires explicit approval of the exact plan in the current conversation. Approval must identify the plan (plan ID, or the target IDs/tier and sizes that were shown). "Clean everything" is not approval.
4. **Tier 3** actions (hibernation, pagefile, app uninstalls) are not targets in `targets.json` and are never performed by these scripts. They need separate, explicit consent and usually a different tool.

`Invoke-Cleanup.ps1 -Apply` rejects plans older than one hour. It re-checks blocked processes and admin state at apply time. It cannot detect a restart or a change to `targets.json`; treat approval as stale after either and regenerate the plan.

## Protected paths

The allowlist in `targets.json` is the primary control. The path guard is defense in depth.

`Test-SafePath` rejects:

- drive roots (`C:\`)
- these exact paths: `%SystemRoot%`, `System32`, `SysWOW64`, `WinSxS`, `servicing`, `Installer`
- `Program Files`, `Program Files (x86)`, `ProgramData`
- the user profile root and `Desktop`, `Documents`, `Downloads`, `Pictures`, `Videos`, `Music`, `OneDrive`
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` roots
- `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh`, `%USERPROFILE%\.config`
- any path containing `..`
- a target path that is itself a reparse point
- any path shallower than three segments

The guard checks each planned target path. Wildcards in `targets.json` are expanded to concrete paths before the apply-time guard runs, so each matched path is checked. The guard does not independently screen every descendant, so do not add a target under a protected directory. `%SystemRoot%\Temp`, `%SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download`, `%SystemRoot%\Minidump\*.dmp`, `%SystemRoot%\LiveKernelReports\*.dmp`, and `%SystemRoot%\MEMORY.DMP` are the only allowlisted paths under `%SystemRoot%`; they are allowed by the allowlist, not by a general exception.

## Never

- Delete user files, project folders, git repositories, or game saves.
- Delete large files or old installers found by `-DeepScan`. They are review-only; the user decides manually.
- Delete `pagefile.sys`, `hiberfil.sys`, or `swapfile.sys` directly. Use the supported OS command and explicit consent.
- Run `DISM /ResetBase` automatically. It removes the ability to uninstall updates.
- Edit the registry, scheduled tasks, services, or firewall to "finish" a cleanup.
- Force-kill browsers or editors to unlock caches.
- Empty the Recycle Bin without approval; it is irreversible.

## Deletion mechanics

- `Remove-CleanupContents` deletes **children** of a target directory, never the directory itself.
- `Remove-CleanupFile` deletes only the exact file or wildcard match. It never recurses into a matched directory.
- Wildcard paths are expanded immediately before measuring, planning, and applying. A match that no longer exists at apply time is skipped.
- Exclusions are resolved to full paths and compared case-insensitively against direct children.
- Locked files are skipped and reported; they are not retried aggressively.
- Every planned filesystem target path is re-validated during apply, not only when the plan was built.
- `Invoke-Cleanup.ps1` ignores the `paths` recorded in the plan and re-expands paths from `targets.json`. Do not edit that file between plan and apply.

## System tools

- Prefer `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore` for reporting.
- `StartComponentCleanup` is tier 2; it can take 10-30 minutes.
- `dism-component-cleanup` has no per-target byte estimate; the report shows 0 bytes. Use `-IncludeDism` for component-store analysis.
- Windows Update and Delivery Optimization caches are safe to clear but need admin; pending updates may download again.
- Windows crash dumps (`MEMORY.DMP`, `Minidump`, `LiveKernelReports`) are tier 2 because deleting them loses diagnostic evidence.
- Use Storage Sense or `cleanmgr` as OS-native alternatives when appropriate. `Windows.old` is recommendation-only; use Settings > System > Storage or Disk Cleanup.
- Do not hand-delete inside `WinSxS`.

## Reporting honesty

- Report measured bytes, not estimates.
- Per-item `freedBytes` is measured for file-based targets. Recycle Bin and DISM report 0 per item; use the net free-space delta.
- Deep-scan results are not cleanup targets. Report them separately and never add them to the cleanup total.
- Some "freed" space may be offset by servicing or application writes; show the net free-space delta.
- Hardlinks, sparse files, and junctions can make logical sizes differ from disk usage. Do not promise the logical total.
- If a cleanup frees less than expected, say so and stop. Do not escalate.
